body.heading: Proposed amendments
body.motion: Hon Paul Goldsmith, in Committee, to move the following amendments:

prov.label: 13AAA
prov.heading: Section 7B amended (Attorney-General’s consent required where jurisdiction claimed under section 7A)

para.text: In section 7B(1) and (2), after 98A,, insert section 98D,.

prov.label: 17A
prov.heading: Section 98F amended (Attorney-General’s consent to prosecutions required)

para.text: In section 98F(1) and (2), delete or section 98D.

sop.para.text: In Part 1, in the subpart 5 heading, replace corrections officers (page 10, line 27) with front-line corrections workers.
In clause 21, delete the definition of corrections officer (page 10, lines 30 to 31).
In clause 21, after the definition of first responder (page 11, after line 6), insert:

para.text: front-line corrections worker means a person—

who has a statutory role or responsibility under subpart 1 of Part 2 of the Corrections Act 2004 (apart from the Minister of Corrections, the chief executive of the Department of Corrections (Corrections), or the Commissioner of Police):
who—
is party to one of the following types of contracts:
an employment agreement between the person and the chief executive of Corrections:
an employment agreement between the person and an entity that has entered into a prison management contract under section 198 of the Corrections Act 2004 (a prison management contractor):
a contract between the person and the chief executive of Corrections:
a contract between the person and a prison management contractor; and
has a duty under that employment agreement or contract that requires direct, in-person interaction with any person under the control or supervision of Corrections:
who—
holds a practising certificate under the Health Practitioners Competence Assurance Act 2003; and

provides healthcare services to any person under the control or supervision of Corrections in circumstances where Corrections or a prison management contractor has facilitated the provision of those services
person under the control or supervision of Corrections means—
an offender as defined in section 3(1) of the Corrections Act 2004:
a person detained or monitored under the Immigration Act 2009:
a person subject to an order or granted Police bail under the Bail Act 2000:
a person subject to electronic monitoring under any legislation:
a person subject to an order under the Public Safety (Public Protection Orders) Act 2014 or the Terrorism Suppression (Control Orders) Act 2019

Before subpart 1 of Part 2 (page 13, before line 5), insert:

para.text: This subpart amends the Criminal Procedure Act 2011.
After section 110, insert:

amend.crosshead: Part of manslaughter by strike to head or neck charge proved

prov.label: 110A
prov.heading: Part of manslaughter by strike to head or neck charge proved

para.text: On a charge of manslaughter by strike to head or neck under section 171A of the Crimes Act 1961, the jury—
may, if the evidence proves manslaughter but does not prove manslaughter by strike to head or neck, find the defendant guilty of manslaughter; but
may not on that charge, except in accordance with section 178(2) of the Crimes Act 1961 (which relates to infanticide), find the defendant guilty of any other offence.

para.text: This Amendment Paper amends the Crimes Amendment Bill (the Bill) to—

expand the provisions of the Bill relating to offences against first responders and corrections officers to cover persons who directly work with persons under the control or supervision of the Department of Corrections (clauses 21 to 24):

amend the Crimes Act 1961 (the Act) to no longer require the Attorney-General’s consent to bring proceedings for human trafficking under section 98D of the Act unless the offence is alleged to have occurred entirely outside of New Zealand (in which case sections 7A and 7B of the Act apply) (new clauses 13AAA and 17A):

amend the Criminal Procedure Act 2011 to permit a jury to make a finding of manslaughter under section 171 of the Act if a defendant is charged with manslaughter by strike to the head or neck under new section 171A, in circumstances where the jury is satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that the elements of manslaughter under section 171, but not all of the elements of manslaughter by strike to the head or neck under new section 171A, are established (new subpart 1AAA of Part 2 of the Bill).
Consequential amendments are also made to the Bill to reflect those changes, and several minor technical errors in the Schedule are corrected.
The Ministry of Justice considers that a departmental disclosure statement is not required to be prepared for this Amendment Paper.
